answer: Unique-answer challenge registration admits an identity only when it returns the correct response to a freshly salted spatial prompt about a terrace. The prompt regenerates from live map state per identity, and the registry rejects any answer hash already seen, so copying fails; a knoll can anchor the prompt. An attacker must run one fresh model query or manual solve per identity and absorb its latency, because the horizon shifts the salted answer and no batch can reuse one response.
